subject: Deployment mode follow-up: migration & mode selection (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Eleanor Park <eleanor.park@novahealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment mode follow-up: migration & mode selection (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)

Hi Eleanor — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and next steps from today's discovery: 

1) Current state: Nova Health is using a mix of a hosted LLM API (Provider A) for new features and an internal self-hosted cluster for sensitive workloads. You're evaluating a migration strategy to reduce per-token cost and get more predictable latency for real-time clinical assistant features.

2) Primary success criteria we heard:
- <15% regression in prompt accuracy vs Provider A (we'll run evals)
- <150ms P95 inference for short-turn chat (90–256 tokens)
- Predictable monthly spend (forecastable committed capacity)
- SOC2 evidence and VPC options for PHI workflows

3) Deployment modes we recommend for consideration (per our call):
- Hosted API: fastest to production, works well for non-PHI, spikes handled by us, usage-based pricing.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU capacity for predictable throughput and lower unit cost for stable traffic (good fit if you need higher throughput and cost predictability).
- Private (VPC / on-prem): customer-managed network, KMS/HSM options, SOC2 & compliance-friendly (best for regulated PHI workloads or strict data residency).

4) Migration considerations specific to Nova Health:
- Lift from Provider A: test parity on a representative prompt set (we can run side-by-side evals).
- Lift from self-hosted cluster: we typically recommend a phased routing approach (start with Hosted for non-PHI, move steadier traffic to Dedicated, then cutover PHI to Private).

Attachments: redwood-deployment-modes-cheatsheet.pdf (summary), SOC2-type2-summary.pdf.

Next steps:
- I'll share the migration checklist + eval plan (attached).
- Stephanie: can you confirm estimated sizing and a rough Dedicated cost example for their 200 RPS peak pattern?
- Eleanor: could you share a small evaluation prompt set (5–10 canonical prompts) and a ballpark monthly token estimate?

Thanks — I'll follow up with the checklist and a proposed timeline.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

From: Eleanor Park <eleanor.park@novahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up: migration & mode selection (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)

Thanks Marissa — very helpful recap. A couple quick clarifications: 

- Our PHI workflows must remain in our VPC or on-prem stack for now (legal requirement). Non-PHI can go to a hosted service.
- Peak pattern is closer to 180–220 RPS (95th percentile spikes during morning triage). Average is ~40 RPS.
- We'll pull together the 8 canonical prompts by EOD Friday and a token estimate (monthly).

On the migration ask: would you recommend starting with Hosted for non-PHI and Dedicated for the steady mid-tier traffic, then Private for PHI? Or is it better to start Dedicated + Private and route spikes to Hosted? We're trying to minimize end-user latency during cutover.

—Eleanor
Platform Lead, Nova Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Eleanor Park <eleanor.park@novahealth.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up: migration & mode selection (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)

Hi Eleanor — thanks, that pattern info is perfect. High-level recommendation (short):

- Phase 1 (0–6 weeks): Hosted for non-PHI, run parity evals and collect traffic profiles. This minimizes time-to-value and lets us validate model parity without touching your infra.

- Phase 2 (6–12 weeks): Provision Dedicated capacity sized to handle baseline + expected growth (covers the 40 RPS average and much of the 95th percentile). Route steady traffic to Dedicated; configure smart routing so Hosted handles transient spikes. This reduces cost vs pure Hosted and keeps latency predictable.

- Phase 3 (12–20 weeks): Private/VPC onboarding for PHI workflows. Once Private is live, migrate PHI routes there. We provide rolling cutover tooling and can keep auditing enabled to validate parity post-migration.

Looping in Stephanie for sizing and cost examples.

Marissa

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Eleanor Park <eleanor.park@novahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up: migration & mode selection (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)

Hi Eleanor — quick sizing notes based on the numbers Marissa shared and similar customers: 

- Baseline (40 RPS avg; 180–220 RPS peaks): Dedicated pool suggestion = 4 x A100-equivalent instances with burst autoscale to handle short-term spikes (policy to scale up to 8 for <5 min bursts). That matches the P95 latency target for 90–256 token responses with our medium-sized model.
- Cost: rough committed monthly estimate for Dedicated (4 reserved units) ~ $XX,XXX / month (I'll send a formal estimate in the next doc). Hosted per-token cost will be higher for sustained steady traffic — we can show a 30–45% cost reduction when moving steady-state to Dedicated vs pure Hosted at your volume.
- Private: depends on on-prem infra; we support both VPC-hosted Private and customer-managed on-prem. For VPC, we'll need network peering details + KMS integration and ~3 weeks for onboarding. For on-prem, plan for 6–8 weeks for packaging and validation.

Migration playbook summary:
- Step A: run side-by-side evals (we'll take your prompt set; we can run against Provider A + Redwood hosted).
- Step B: small canary on Hosted with traffic shadowing to Dedicated to validate latency/cost.
- Step C: expand Dedicated capacity, enable routing rules, then enable Private for PHI cutover.

I'll follow up with the sizing workbook and a sample Dedicated pricing sheet. Happy to hop on a quick tech session to walk through the canary plan — Marissa, do you want to propose a time next week?

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
